title: Ephemeral crediting for partial resets and idempotent mid-period accounting
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Background: During mid-cycle reserved-pool rebalances and tenant migrations we observe transient mismatches between the inflight usage ledger and on-disk quota anchors. This causes either temporary double-debiting or loss of provisional credits when a tenant's allocation is partially reset or re-anchored across regions. Problem: existing reset operations are coarse (full-epoch resets) and not idempotent at the operation level; retries and out-of-order events from cross-region services lead to missed backfills and customer-visible overages. Goal: implement an ephemeral-crediting layer and idempotent partial-reset primitive so mid-period operations (rebalances, partial reservations, manual adjustments) can execute safely without producing permanent accounting errors or customer-visible spikes.
technical_design:
We will add a lightweight provisional ledger overlay that sits between the usage accumulator and the canonical tenant quota anchor. Key components: 1) Snapshot checkpoint: when a partial-reset or rebalancing event is initiated, we create a time-bounded snapshot (snapshot_id, epoch_hash, vector_clock) stored in the shadow-ledger bucket. Snapshots are cheap protobufs with a hash to detect identical retries. 2) Provisional credits: apply ephemeral credits in the provisional ledger namespace (tenant_id, snapshot_id) which override derived remaining quota for reads but do not immediately mutate the canonical anchor. 3) Idempotent operation tokens: every mid-period operation must include an operation_token (uuid) and snapshots are keyed by operation_token to guarantee idempotence. 4) Reconcile/backfill worker: a durable worker consumes snapshot tombstones and tries to reconcile provisional credits into the canonical ledger using a compare-and-swap flow with optimistic concurrency. If a conflict is detected (concurrent reset), the worker merges deltas deterministically by epoch sequence. 5) Lease fencing: operations must acquire a short-lived lease per-tenant to avoid simultaneous partial resets. Lease acquisition is best-effort; if lease can't be acquired we fall back to queuing the operation and marking the snapshot as "deferred". 6) Observability: emit events for snapshot_created, provisional_applied, reconcile_started, reconcile_conflict, reconcile_committed, reconcile_aborted. 7) Rollback & tombstones: provisional entries expire after X hours (configurable), and a tombstone record ensures workers do not double-commit. 8) Backfill safety: when reconciling, we compute delta = canonical_usage + provisional_delta - expected_anchor; if abs(delta) > safety_threshold (configurable in tenant metadata), flag for manual review and do not auto-commit. Implementation notes:
- Use existing shadow-ledger S3 prefix with per-region replication tags.
- Keep in-memory cache eviction tuned to avoid memory pressure on runtime path.
- Respect timezone-aware epoch boundaries: all snapshots include UTC timestamps and tenant timezone offsets for accurate mid-night prorations.
- Provide a small feature-flag to enable ephemeral-crediting per enterprise customer.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Canary tenants (small set) see zero customer-visible overages during simulated partial resets and rebalances in staging.
2) The partial-reset API is idempotent: retrying the same operation_token produces identical ledger state and no duplicate credits (verify with unit and integration tests).
3) Reconcile worker commits or tombstones provisional entries within SLA: median commit latency < 3 minutes for typical backlog, 95th < 15 minutes under load test load.
4) Telemetry emitted for each main lifecycle event and reconciliations surface a reconciliation_success_rate >= 99.9% on canary tenants.
5) No unhandled exceptions or panics when the canonical anchor changes during reconcile; conflicts are resolved via deterministic merge algorithm.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (shadow mode): implement provisional ledger and snapshot creation; do not affect reads. Run for 2 weeks on internal/test tenants and collect diffs between canonical and provisional read paths.
Phase 2 (canary apply): enable ephemeral-crediting for 5 low-volume enterprise tenants; provisional credits used in reads but reconciliation still requires manual review for flagged deltas.
Phase 3 (automated reconcile): enable auto-commit reconcile for tenants with safety_threshold <= configured value; monitor metrics and throttles; keep rollback hooks available.
Phase 4 (rollout wide): enable per-tenant feature-flag by default and remove long-lived shadow artifacts after two billing cycles.
Rollback: disable feature-flag and run reconciliation job to collapse provisional credits into canonical anchors or produce manual adjustments if necessary.
qa_steps: Unit tests for idempotent partial-reset with identical operation_token (no duplicate credits).
Integration test: simulate cross-region duplicate reset events with out-of-order delivery; assert final ledger equals single reset semantics.
Load test: create backlog of 50k provisional snapshots and ensure reconcile worker processes them within expected SLA under throttling rules.
Manual test: enable canary on internal tenant, run synthetic rebalances and verify UI and billing metrics unchanged for customers.
Chaos test: kill reconcile worker mid-commit and ensure tombstones prevent duplicate commits on restart.
